# Updates in Cooperative AI

Chandler Smith (University of Oxford, Oxford Martin AI Governance Initiative, Cooperative AI Foundation)

Qi Guo (Cooperative AI Foundation)

16:00-17:00 UTC 5 November 2026

Chandler Smith is a DPhil Affiliate of the Oxford Martin AI Governance Initiative, an incoming DPhil candidate in Engineering Science at the University of Oxford’s Torr Vision Group , and a CAIF PhD Fellow. Before beginning his DPhil, Chandler was a Research Engineer at CAIF, where he contributed to technical research on multi-agent systems. He received a Foresight Institute AI Safety grant and consulted with IQT’s applied research teams on AI, multi-agent systems, and AI infrastructure. He was also a scholar in the ML Alignment & Theory Scholars (MATS) program. Chandler is particularly interested in agent infrastructure and the risks that emerge from multi-agent interactions. This includes challenges related to AI-AI negotiation, scalable oversight, and the benchmarking of agentic behaviour.

‍

Qi Guo is a Research Engineer at CAIF, where she supports engineering for inter-agent influence evaluation. She holds a bachelor's degree in Software Engineering from Peking University. Prior to joining CAIF, Qi built up her engineering background through roles at Microsoft and the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). Qi developed her foundation in AI safety research with a particular focus on evaluations through research fellowships including ARENA and MARS. Her recent work centres on exploring key agent properties, establishing which traits enable AI agents to remain safe and reliable when deployed in complex, real-world environments.
